Pattern Decomposition (Gullí).name: Pattern Decomposition (Gullí)
Pattern Decomposition (Gullí).principle: Any agent behavior decomposes into a small catalog of reusable patterns (ReAct, reflection, planning, routing, multi-agent coordination) — build from the catalog, don't invent bespoke loops.
Pattern Decomposition (Gullí).when_to_use: Designing any new agent: first ask "which of the 21 patterns is this?", only write custom orchestration when none fits.

RAG Maturity Ladder.name: RAG Maturity Ladder
RAG Maturity Ladder.principle: RAG is not one technique but a ladder — naive keyword → vector search → modular retrieval components → GraphRAG/MAS-RAG — and each rung has a cost; climb only when the current rung measurably fails.
RAG Maturity Ladder.when_to_use: Whenever retrieval quality is questioned: identify the current rung and the specific failure before upgrading (e.g., TF-IDF → embeddings only if keyword recall is the proven bottleneck).

Memory ≠ One Thing.name: Memory ≠ One Thing
Memory ≠ One Thing.principle: Agent memory splits into distinct types (short-term/context, long-term episodic, semantic, shared blackboard) with different write policies — conflating them causes both context bloat and forgetting.
Memory ≠ One Thing.when_to_use: When an agent "forgets" or its context overflows: diagnose which memory type is missing/overloaded rather than just enlarging the prompt.

Context Engineering Over Prompt Tweaking.name: Context Engineering Over Prompt Tweaking
Context Engineering Over Prompt Tweaking.principle: What's *inside* the context window (selection, compression, structure — context-as-specification) determines output quality more than wording tricks; optimize the payload, not the phrasing.
Context Engineering Over Prompt Tweaking.when_to_use: Before rewording any underperforming prompt: audit what facts the model actually receives (the Jyoti lordship bug — hallucination from missing data, not bad wording — is the canonical local example).

Document-Completion Frame (Berryman).name: Document-Completion Frame (Berryman)
Document-Completion Frame (Berryman).principle: An LLM is a document completer seeing tokens, not letters or intent — hallucinations, repetition traps, and format drift are all consequences; design prompts as documents whose most-likely continuation is the answer you want.
Document-Completion Frame (Berryman).when_to_use: Debugging any weird LLM output (markdown fences, truncation, made-up fields): ask "what document does the model think it's completing?"

Tool Lifecycle Discipline.name: Tool Lifecycle Discipline
Tool Lifecycle Discipline.principle: Tools follow a lifecycle — create → define (schema) → select → call → process output — and most tool failures are at the *definition* and *output-processing* ends, not the call itself.
Tool Lifecycle Discipline.when_to_use: When an agent misuses tools: tighten schemas/descriptions and post-process outputs before touching the agent's reasoning loop.

Escalating Autonomy (L0→L5).name: Escalating Autonomy (L0→L5)
Escalating Autonomy (L0→L5).principle: Agent autonomy is a graded ladder (chatbot → tool-user → planner → multi-agent → self-improving); each level adds failure modes, so grant the *lowest* level that achieves the task.
Escalating Autonomy (L0→L5).when_to_use: Scoping any new agent: pick the level deliberately, and require evidence (eval results) before promoting a system up a level.

Grounding Beats Generation.name: Grounding Beats Generation
Grounding Beats Generation.principle: Never let an LLM invent numbers or facts a deterministic computation can supply — compute the fact, hand it to the model as ground truth, and instruct it to cite, not derive.
Grounding Beats Generation.when_to_use: Any pipeline where LLM output includes verifiable claims (prices, placements, dates): add a computed-facts block first (stock_agent grounding + vedic house-lords table are the local proofs).

Evaluator as First-Class Role.name: Evaluator as First-Class Role
Evaluator as First-Class Role.principle: A generation system has four roles — Retriever, Generator, Evaluator, Trainer — and skipping the Evaluator means quality claims are anecdotes; build the eval before trusting the output.
Evaluator as First-Class Role.when_to_use: Before shipping any LLM feature: define the ground-truth check first (the 12-ascendant lordship eval and backtest leak-test pattern).

Framework-Last Selection.name: Framework-Last Selection
Framework-Last Selection.principle: Choose orchestration frameworks (LangGraph, CrewAI, AutoGen, raw SDK) by the coordination topology the task needs — not by popularity; simple sequential/parallel flows rarely justify a framework at all.
Framework-Last Selection.when_to_use: At project start: sketch the agent topology on paper first; adopt a framework only when the topology (cycles, handoffs, shared state) demands it.
